## 1. Constitution of India: education-related provisions (शिक्षा संबंधी संवैधानिक प्रावधान)

- Structure: Part III Fundamental Rights (मूल अधिकार, Art 12–35); Part IV Directive Principles (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्त्व, Art 36–51); Part IVA Fundamental Duties (मूल कर्तव्य, Art 51A).
- **Art 21A** (शिक्षा का अधिकार): inserted by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**; brought into force on **1 April 2010**, the same day as the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009** (Act 35 of 2009). Text: the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of **six to fourteen years** "in such manner as the State may, by law, determine".
- **Art 45**: originally directed free and compulsory education for all children until 14 within ten years of the Constitution. After the 86th Amendment it reads: the State shall endeavour to provide **early childhood care and education (ECCE) for all children until they complete the age of six years**.
- **Art 51A(k)**: the **eleventh Fundamental Duty**, added by the 86th Amendment: the **parent or guardian** must provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years. (The first ten duties came through the 42nd Amendment, 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.)
- **Art 46**: the State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, in particular SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.
- **Art 29**: protection of interests of minorities. 29(1): any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture has the right to conserve it. 29(2): no citizen shall be denied admission to a State-maintained or State-aided institution on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language.
- **Art 30**: religious or linguistic minorities may establish and administer educational institutions of their choice; 30(1A) (44th Amendment, 1978) protects compensation on acquisition of minority institution property; 30(2) bars discrimination in State aid.
- **Art 28**: no religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds; in aided/recognised institutions attendance at religious instruction needs consent (of the guardian for minors).
- **Art 350A**: every State and local authority shall endeavour to provide adequate facilities for **instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage** to children of linguistic minority groups; the President may issue directions. **Art 350B**: a **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities** (भाषाई अल्पसंख्यकों के लिए विशेष अधिकारी) appointed by the President, reporting to the President; reports are laid before Parliament and sent to State governments. Both were inserted by the **7th Amendment Act, 1956** (States Reorganisation), not by the 42nd.
- **Art 15(5)** (93rd Amendment, 2005): special provision for SEBC/SC/ST admission to private educational institutions, aided or unaided, other than minority institutions. **Art 15(6)/16(6)** (103rd Amendment, 2019): up to 10% for EWS.
- Language articles: **Art 343** Hindi in Devanagari as the official language of the Union; **Art 351** directive to promote Hindi; **Eighth Schedule: 22 languages** (14 originally; Sindhi 1967; Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali 1992; Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali 2003 by the 92nd Amendment).
- **Seventh Schedule**: education was a **State List** subject until the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** moved it to the **Concurrent List, Entry 25 of List III**: "Education, including technical education, medical education and universities, subject to the provisions of entries 63, 64, 65 and 66 of List I; vocational and technical training of labour." **Union List Entry 66**: co-ordination and determination of standards in institutions for higher education or research and scientific and technical institutions. Entries 63–65 cover institutions of national importance (BHU, AMU, Delhi University and others declared by Parliament), Union agencies for professional/vocational training, and the like. **Eleventh Schedule** (73rd Amendment, 1992; Panchayats; 29 subjects) includes education including primary and secondary schools, technical training and vocational education, adult and non-formal education, libraries. **Twelfth Schedule** (74th Amendment; Municipalities; 18 subjects) includes promotion of cultural, educational and aesthetic aspects.

| 73rd/74th | 1992 | Panchayats (11th Schedule) and Municipalities (12th Schedule) with education subjects |
| 86th | 2002 | Art 21A inserted; Art 45 substituted (ECCE under six); Art 51A(k) added |

| 103rd | 2019 | 10% EWS reservation (Art 15(6), 16(6)) |

## 2. Polity basics (राजव्यवस्था)

- Constituent Assembly first met **9 Dec 1946**; Constitution adopted **26 Nov 1949** (Constitution Day / संविधान दिवस), commenced **26 Jan 1950**. Drafting Committee chair: **Dr B.R. Ambedkar**. Originally 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules; now 12 Schedules.
- **Fundamental Duties**: 42nd Amendment 1976, Swaran Singh Committee, ten duties; eleventh (51A(k)) by 86th Amendment 2002. They are **non-justiciable** (not directly enforceable by courts).
- **Art 32**: right to constitutional remedies, called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Ambedkar. Writs: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto. **Art 226**: High Court writs.
- **President** (Art 52–62): elected by an electoral college of elected MPs and elected MLAs of States, plus the **NCT of Delhi and Puducherry (added by the 70th Amendment Act, 1992)**. Term 5 years; impeachment Art 61.
- **Supreme Court** Art 124; **High Courts** Art 214; **Comptroller and Auditor General** Art 148; **UPSC** Art 315–323 (recruitment to Union services; the Vice Principal CRT is conducted by UPSC under Art 320).
- **Delhi**: the **69th Amendment Act, 1991** inserted **Art 239AA** and **239AB**, making the Union Territory of Delhi the **National Capital Territory (NCT)** with a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers; the **GNCTD Act, 1991** supplements it. Assembly: **70 members**, all directly elected (first Assembly 1993). Council of Ministers: **not more than 10% of the Assembly** (i.e. 7, including the CM); CM appointed by the President. The Assembly may legislate on State List and Concurrent List matters applicable to UTs **except Entries 1 (public order), 2 (police) and 18 (land)** of the State List. In case of repugnancy, Parliament's law prevails. Head: **Lieutenant Governor** (Administrator under Art 239). **Delhi Police** reports to the MHA.
- Delhi representation: **7 Lok Sabha** and **3 Rajya Sabha** seats. **Delhi High Court** established **31 Oct 1966** (Delhi High Court Act, 1966). **11 revenue districts** (since Sept 2012). The three municipal corporations were re-unified as the **Municipal Corporation of Delhi** by the DMC (Amendment) Act, 2022 (250 wards); **NDMC** (New Delhi Municipal Council Act, 1994) and the Delhi Cantonment Board are separate.
- Other amendments to know: **101st (2016)** GST, effective 1 July 2017; **104th (2019)** extended SC/ST reservation in legislatures to 2030 and ended Anglo-Indian nominated seats; **106th (2023)** Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam: one-third of seats for women in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, to take effect after the delimitation that follows the first Census after commencement.

## 3. History of education in India: commissions and policies (शिक्षा आयोग एवं नीतियाँ)

### Ancient and medieval
- Vedic gurukul system; Buddhist viharas. **Takshashila**; **Nalanda** (founded by **Kumaragupta I** of the Gupta dynasty, 5th century CE; Xuanzang studied there in the 7th century; UNESCO World Heritage Site 2016); **Vikramshila** (founded by **Dharmapala**, Pala dynasty); **Vallabhi** (Gujarat); Odantapuri. Medieval maktabs and madrasas; **Firoz Shah Tughlaq's madrasa at Hauz Khas, Delhi**.

### British period
| Year | Event | Key point |
|---|---|---|
| 1781 | Calcutta Madrasa (Warren Hastings) | First British educational institution |
| 1791 | Benares Sanskrit College (Jonathan Duncan) | |
| 1813 | **Charter Act** | **Rs 1 lakh per year** for education; first acceptance of State responsibility |
| 1817 | Hindu College, Calcutta (David Hare, Ram Mohan Roy) | Later Presidency College |
| 1835 | **Macaulay's Minute** | English as medium; "downward filtration" |
| 1854 | **Wood's Despatch** (Charles Wood) | "**Magna Carta of English education in India**"; recommended universities at Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (set up **1857**), Department of Public Instruction in each province, grants-in-aid, teacher training, women's education, vernacular at school level |
| 1882 | **Hunter Commission** (Indian Education Commission; Sir W.W. Hunter; Viceroy Lord Ripon) | Stress on **primary education** and its transfer to **local bodies**; two secondary streams ('A' literary, 'B' vocational); grant-in-aid for private effort |
| 1902–04 | Raleigh Commission; **Indian Universities Act, 1904** (Curzon) | Tighter government control of universities |
| 1917–19 | **Sadler Commission** (Calcutta University Commission; Michael Sadler) | 12-year school course, intermediate stage, 3-year degree, Board of Secondary and Intermediate Education; led to Dhaka, Lucknow, Aligarh universities |
| 1929 | **Hartog Committee** | Consolidation over expansion; **wastage and stagnation** in primary education |
| 1937 | **Wardha Scheme / Basic Education / Nai Talim** (Gandhi; **Dr Zakir Husain Committee**) | Craft-centred, self-supporting, mother tongue, ages 7–14 |
| 1944 | **Sargent Report** (CABE; John Sargent; "Post-War Educational Development in India") | Universal free compulsory education for **6–14 within 40 years**; pre-primary for 3–6; **Kher Committee (1948) cut the period to 16 years** |

## 4. Educationists and reformers (शिक्षाविद् एवं समाज सुधारक)

- **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**: Hindu College (1817, with David Hare), Vedanta College (1825), Brahmo Sabha (1828). **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**: Bengali primer *Barna Parichay*; girls' schools; Widow Remarriage Act 1856.
- **Savitribai and Jyotirao Phule**: first girls' school run by Indians at Bhidewada, Pune (**1848**); Satyashodhak Samaj (1873). Savitribai is honoured as India's first woman teacher (3 Jan).
- **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan**: Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh (1875), which became **AMU (1920)**. **Swami Dayanand Saraswati**: Arya Samaj (1875); DAV movement (1886). **Swami Vivekananda**: "Education is the manifestation of the perfection already in man"; National Youth Day 12 Jan. **Annie Besant**: Central Hindu College, Varanasi (1898). **Madan Mohan Malaviya**: **BHU (1916)**.
- **Rabindranath Tagore**: Santiniketan school (1901), **Visva-Bharati (1921)**; Nobel Prize in Literature 1913. **Mahatma Gandhi**: Nai Talim (1937), Gujarat Vidyapith (1920). **Sri Aurobindo**: integral education. **J. Krishnamurti**: Rishi Valley School (1926). **Gijubhai Badheka**: pre-primary pioneer at Dakshinamurti, Bhavnagar.
- **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**: first Union Education Minister (1947–58); birthday **11 Nov = National Education Day** (राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा दिवस, since 2008); set up UGC, IIT Kharagpur (1951), Sangeet Natak, Lalit Kala and Sahitya Akademis. **Dr S. Radhakrishnan**: University Education Commission; **Teachers' Day 5 Sept**; first Vice-President, second President. **Dr Zakir Husain**: Jamia Millia Islamia; Wardha scheme committee; third President. **Dr B.R. Ambedkar**: "Educate, Agitate, Organise"; People's Education Society (1945).
- **Jamia Millia Islamia**: founded at Aligarh in 1920, moved to Delhi 1925, Central University 1988. **University of Delhi**: 1922. **JNU**: 1969. **IIT Delhi**: 1961 (IIT status 1963). **AIIMS**: 1956. **IGNOU**: 1985.

## 5. Delhi-specific GK (दिल्ली विशेष)

- **Capital**: shift from Calcutta to Delhi announced at the **Delhi Durbar, 12 Dec 1911** (George V). New Delhi planned by **Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker**; inaugurated **13 Feb 1931**. Parliament House 1927; Viceroy's House is now Rashtrapati Bhavan.
- **Historic cities of Delhi**: Lal Kot / Qila Rai Pithora (Tomars, Prithviraj Chauhan); **Siri (Alauddin Khalji)**; **Tughlaqabad (Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq)**; **Jahanpanah (Muhammad bin Tughlaq)**; **Firozabad / Firoz Shah Kotla (Firoz Shah Tughlaq)**; **Dinpanah / Purana Qila (Humayun; Sher Shah's Shergarh)**; **Shahjahanabad (Shah Jahan, 1639; Red Fort, Jama Masjid 1656)**; New Delhi (British). **Qutb Minar**: begun by **Qutb-ud-din Aibak** (1199), completed by **Iltutmish**; top storeys repaired by Firoz Shah Tughlaq; Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and the Gupta-era Iron Pillar stand in the complex. **Humayun's Tomb** (1570, Haji Begum; first Mughal garden tomb). Hauz Khas tank (Alauddin) and madrasa (Firoz Shah). Lotus Temple 1986; Akshardham 2005.
- **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Delhi (3)**: **Qutb Minar and its Monuments (1993)**, **Humayun's Tomb (1993)**, **Red Fort Complex (2007)**. Jantar Mantar Delhi is **not** inscribed (Jaipur's Jantar Mantar is, 2010). India's total: **43** after the Moidams of the Ahom dynasty (2024); the Maratha Military Landscapes were inscribed in July 2025 as the **44th**.
- **Geography**: Delhi is bounded by **Haryana** (north, west, south) and **Uttar Pradesh** (east). Area about **1,483 sq km**. The **Delhi Ridge is the northern extension of the Aravalli Range**. The **Yamuna** enters at **Palla** in the north; the Wazirabad–Okhla stretch is the most polluted. Semi-arid climate with extreme summers and winters. State bird: **house sparrow** (2012).
- **Census 2011 (Delhi)**: population **1.68 crore**; literacy **86.2%**; sex ratio **868**; highest population density in India (about 11,320 per sq km).
- **School education administration**: **Directorate of Education (DoE), GNCTD** (शिक्षा निदेशालय), Old Secretariat, Delhi-110054; **Delhi School Education Act, 1973 (Act 18 of 1973) and Delhi School Education Rules, 1973** (DSEAR); **Delhi RTE Rules, 2011**; **Delhi School Education (Transparency in Fixation and Regulation of Fees) Act, 2025**; **SCERT Delhi (1988)** and DIETs; **Delhi Board of School Education (DBSE), 2021**. School types: Sarvodaya Vidyalayas, Rajkiya Pratibha Vikas Vidyalayas (RPVV), Schools of Specialised Excellence (SoSE), **CM SHRI schools (2025)**. 25% EWS/DG entry-level admissions in private unaided schools are run through the DoE online draw.
- **Higher education in Delhi**: University of Delhi (1922), Jamia Millia Islamia (Delhi since 1925), JNU (1969), IIT Delhi (1961), AIIMS (1956), IGNOU (1985), GGSIPU (1998), Ambedkar University Delhi (2008), IIIT-Delhi (2008), DTU (DCE 1941; university 2009), NSUT, Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University (2020), Delhi Teachers University (2022).
- **Sports**: Delhi hosted the first Asian Games (**1951**) and the 1982 Asian Games; **Commonwealth Games 2010**.

## 6. Geography basics (भूगोल)

- India: area **32.87 lakh sq km**, **2.4%** of the world's land, **7th largest** country; about 17.5% of world population (most populous country per UN estimates since 2023). Latitude 8°4'N–37°6'N; longitude 68°7'E–97°25'E.
- **IST = 82°30'E** (passes through **Mirzapur, UP**); IST is 5 h 30 min ahead of GMT. **Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N)** passes through **8 States**: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram. Delhi lies at about 28.6°N, well north of it.
- **28 States and 8 UTs**: J&K and Ladakh became UTs on **31 Oct 2019**; Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu merged on **26 Jan 2020**.
- Extremes: southernmost point **Indira Point** (Great Nicobar); mainland tip Kanyakumari. Highest peak in India **Kanchenjunga (8,586 m)**. Longest river **Ganga**; **Yamuna** rises at Yamunotri glacier and joins the Ganga at Prayagraj. Largest river island **Majuli** (Assam). Longest coastline **Gujarat**. Largest State Rajasthan, smallest Goa; most populous Uttar Pradesh, least Sikkim. Land neighbours: 7 (Bangladesh longest border, Afghanistan shortest).

## 7. Economy and social issues (अर्थव्यवस्था एवं सामाजिक मुद्दे)

- **Census 2011** (15th Census, 7th after independence): population **121.09 crore**; decadal growth 17.7%; **literacy 74.04%** (male **82.14%**, female **65.46%**); **Kerala highest (94.0%)**, **Bihar lowest (61.8%)**; sex ratio **943**; child sex ratio (0–6) **918**; urban share 31.2%. **Census 2027**: houselisting from April 2026 with **self-enumeration** for the first time; population enumeration in Feb 2027 (reference date 1 March 2027); first digital census; caste enumeration included.
- **Demographic dividend** (जनसांख्यिकीय लाभांश): the growth potential that arises when the **working-age population (15–64)** forms a larger share than dependents (children and elderly); India's median age is about 28, and the window is expected to last until roughly the mid-2050s. Converting it requires investment in health, education and skills (human capital). Related terms: **dependency ratio**, **total fertility rate** (India around 2.0, below replacement 2.1 per NFHS-5).
- **Education spending**: Centre plus States spend roughly 4–4.6% of GDP, against the **6% target** first set by the **Kothari Commission** and repeated in NPE 1968, NPE 1986 and NEP 2020. **Union Budget 2026-27**: Ministry of Education **Rs 1,39,289 crore** (School Education Rs 83,562 crore; Higher Education Rs 55,727 crore), per PRS.
- **Sustainable Development Goals (सतत विकास लक्ष्य)**: adopted by the UN General Assembly in **September 2015** ("Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda"); **17 goals, 169 targets**, horizon **2030**. The MDGs (2000–2015) had 8 goals. **SDG 4 Quality Education** has **10 targets**: 4.1 free, equitable, quality primary and secondary completion; 4.2 ECCE and pre-primary; 4.3 affordable TVET and tertiary; 4.4 skills for employment; 4.5 eliminate gender disparities, equal access for the vulnerable; 4.6 youth and adult literacy and numeracy; 4.7 education for sustainable development and global citizenship; 4.a inclusive, safe facilities; 4.b scholarships; 4.c qualified teachers. **SDG 5** is gender equality. NITI Aayog publishes the **SDG India Index** (Kerala topped the 2023-24 edition).
- **Gender**: **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** launched **22 Jan 2015 at Panipat** (MWCD with MoHFW and MoE); **National Girl Child Day 24 Jan**; **Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas** (2004); **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana** (2015); **PCPNDT Act 1994**; **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act 2006** (girl 18, boy 21); **Dowry Prohibition Act 1961**; **POSH Act 2013** (Internal Committee where 10 or more employees); **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam 2023**. Gender Parity Index in higher education **1.08** (AISHE 2023-24).
- **Children**: **POCSO Act 2012** (child = below 18; gender-neutral; Special Courts; mandatory reporting; 2019 amendment introduced the death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault); **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015** (16–18-year-olds may be tried as adults for heinous offences after a JJB assessment; CWCs; 2021 amendment made the District Magistrate the adoption authority); **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act 2016** (complete ban on employment below 14 except in family enterprises after school hours and as child artists; 14–18 'adolescents' barred from hazardous occupations); **CPCR Act 2005 → NCPCR (2007)** and State commissions (DCPCR in Delhi); **Childline 1098**; **Mid-Day Meal (1995) → PM POSHAN (Sept 2021)**; **ICDS (1975) → Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0**.
- **Inclusion**: **Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016** (in force 19 April 2017; replaced the PwD Act 1995): **21 specified disabilities**; **benchmark disability = 40% or more**; **4% reservation in government posts** (Sec 34); **5% seats in government and aided higher education institutions** (Sec 32); **Sec 31: free education for every child with benchmark disability aged 6–18** in a neighbourhood or special school; Sec 16 duties of educational institutions (inclusive education); **UDID card**; Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities; **Accessible India Campaign (2015)**. **Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019**; **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989**; **Eklavya Model Residential Schools** (Classes 6–12 for ST children); Samagra Shiksha's inclusive education component (CWSN).
- **Literacy**: **ULLAS – Nav Bharat Saksharta Karyakram** (2022–27; non-literates aged 15+; FLNAT test). States/UTs declared **fully literate** (95%+ benchmark): Ladakh (UT, 2024), Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, **Sikkim (5th State, May 2026)** and **Uttarakhand (6th, July 2026)** as reported. Earlier programmes: **National Literacy Mission 1988**, **Saakshar Bharat 2009**. **International Literacy Day 8 Sept**.
- **Poverty and labour**: NITI Aayog **Multidimensional Poverty Index** (headcount fell from 24.85% in 2015-16 to 14.96% in 2019-21); **four Labour Codes** in force from **21 Nov 2025**; **VB-G RAM G Act, 2025** (125 days of guaranteed rural work) replaced MGNREGA from **1 July 2026**, per PIB; **HDR 2025: India ranked 130 of 193** on the HDI.

Indian Nobel laureates (citizens at the time): Tagore 1913, C.V. Raman 1930, Mother Teresa 1979, Amartya Sen 1998, Kailash Satyarthi 2014.

## 9. Science basics (विज्ञान)

- **Human body**: 206 bones in an adult; femur longest, stapes smallest; 32 permanent teeth; blood groups ABO (Karl Landsteiner); O-negative universal donor, AB-positive universal recipient; normal BP about 120/80 mm Hg; normal temperature 37°C (98.6°F); RBC life about 120 days; **insulin** (pancreas) deficiency causes diabetes; **iodine** deficiency causes goitre; **iron** deficiency causes anaemia.
- **Vitamins and deficiency diseases**: **A (retinol) – night blindness/xerophthalmia**; **B1 (thiamine) – beri-beri**; B3 (niacin) – pellagra; B12 – pernicious anaemia; **C (ascorbic acid) – scurvy**; **D – rickets** (children) and osteomalacia (adults; sunlight helps synthesis); K – clotting. Protein-energy malnutrition: kwashiorkor, marasmus.
- **Diseases**: viral – COVID-19, dengue, polio, measles, chickenpox, rabies, AIDS; bacterial – tuberculosis (BCG vaccine), cholera, typhoid, diphtheria, tetanus, leprosy; protozoan – malaria (Plasmodium, female Anopheles); fungal – ringworm. **Mission Indradhanush (2014)** strengthens routine immunisation.
- **Physics and chemistry**: 7 SI base units (m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd); speed of light 3 × 10^8 m/s; speed of sound in air about 343 m/s; pH 7 neutral, below 7 acidic; common salt NaCl, baking soda NaHCO3, washing soda Na2CO3, bleaching powder CaOCl2, dry ice solid CO2, laughing gas N2O; **ozone layer** in the stratosphere (CFCs; Montreal Protocol 1987; Ozone Day 16 Sept); greenhouse gases CO2, CH4, N2O.
- **Space and technology**: ISRO (1969, Vikram Sarabhai); Aryabhata (1975); Chandrayaan-1 (2008, water on Moon), Chandrayaan-2 (2019), **Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole on 23 Aug 2023 (Shiv Shakti Point)**; Mangalyaan (2013); Aditya-L1 (2023); Gaganyaan (human spaceflight programme); **Shubhanshu Shukla**, first Indian on the ISS (Axiom-4, June 2025); NISAR (ISRO–NASA, July 2025). PARAM 8000 (1991) first Indian supercomputer (C-DAC); **Digital India 2015**; IndiaAI Mission 2024.

## Common traps

- **86th (Art 21A) vs 93rd (Art 15(5)) vs 42nd (Concurrent List)**. The 44th Amendment gave Art 30(1A), not Art 21A.
- Art 21A = free and compulsory education **6–14** (Part III). Art 45 now = **ECCE below six** (Part IV). Art 51A(k) = duty of the **parent or guardian** (Part IVA), not of the State.
- **Art 350A** (mother-tongue instruction) vs **Art 350B** (Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities): both from the **7th Amendment 1956**.
- **Entry 25, List III** (education) vs **Entry 66, List I** (standards in higher education).
- **Kothari** gave 10+2+3 and the 6% target; **NPE 1968** adopted them; **NPE 1986** gave Operation Blackboard and Navodaya; **1992** = POA and revised policy (Janardhana Reddy); **Ramamurti 1990** = review.
- **Yashpal 1993** (school curriculum load) vs **Yashpal 2009** (higher education).
- **Sargent 1944 = 40 years**; **Kher 1948 = 16 years**. **Wardha 1937** committee chair was **Zakir Husain**, not Gandhi or Kher.
- **Hunter 1882** (primary and local bodies) vs **Sadler 1917** (Calcutta University, 12-year school) vs **Hartog 1929** (wastage and stagnation).
- Wood's Despatch **1854** recommended the universities; they were founded in **1857**.
- Delhi: **69th Amendment 1991** created the Assembly; **70th Amendment 1992** put Delhi's MLAs in the Presidential electoral college. **70 MLAs**, **at most 7 ministers**; no power over **public order, police, land**.
- Delhi World Heritage Sites: **3**; Jantar Mantar Delhi is not one.
- Census 2011 literacy **74.04%** (2001: 64.8%); Kerala highest, Bihar lowest; Delhi 86.2%.
- RPwD 2016: **21** disabilities; **4%** job reservation (3% was the 1995 Act); **5%** HE seats; **40%** benchmark; free education **6–18** (not 6–14 as in RTE).
- Classical languages **11** (not 6); Eighth Schedule **22**; classical dances **8**.
- SDGs adopted **2015**, horizon 2030; MDGs were 2000–2015. **SDG 4 has 10 targets**.
- Age limits: POCSO child **below 18**; RTE **6–14**; child labour ban **below 14**, adolescents **14–18**; JJ Act heinous offences **16–18**.
- Days: National Education Day **11 Nov** (Azad) vs Teachers' Day **5 Sept** (Radhakrishnan) vs World Teachers' Day **5 Oct** vs International Day of Education **24 Jan** vs International Literacy Day **8 Sept**.
- Nalanda was founded by **Kumaragupta I**; Harsha was a patron; Dharmapala founded **Vikramshila**.

quick_facts: Art 21A (free and compulsory education, ages 6–14) was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 and came into force on 1 April 2010 with the RTE Act 2009.
After the 86th Amendment, Art 45 directs the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete six years.
Art 51A(k): duty of the parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to the child/ward aged 6–14; it is the 11th Fundamental Duty.
Art 350A (mother-tongue instruction at primary stage) and Art 350B (Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities) were inserted by the 7th Amendment Act, 1956.
The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 moved 'Education' from the State List to the Concurrent List (Entry 25, List III); Entry 66 of the Union List covers standards in higher education.
Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment (Swaran Singh Committee); they are not enforceable by courts.
Delhi: 69th Amendment Act 1991 inserted Art 239AA; Assembly of 70 members; Council of Ministers not more than 10% of the Assembly; no power over public order, police and land.
The 70th Amendment Act, 1992 included MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry in the electoral college for the President.
Delhi has 7 Lok Sabha and 3 Rajya Sabha seats; the Delhi High Court was established on 31 Oct 1966; Delhi has 11 revenue districts.
Delhi School Education Act, 1973 (Act 18 of 1973) and Rules 1973 govern recognised schools in Delhi; DBSE was set up in 2021.
UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Delhi: Qutb Minar and its Monuments (1993), Humayun's Tomb (1993), Red Fort Complex (2007).
Kothari Commission (1964–66, D.S. Kothari) recommended 10+2+3, the common school system and 6% of national income on education; NPE 1968 adopted them.
NPE 1986 (Rajiv Gandhi) launched Operation Blackboard and Navodaya Vidyalayas; it was revised in 1992 after the Acharya Ramamurti review (1990).
Sargent Report (1944) aimed at universal free compulsory education for 6–14 within 40 years; the Kher Committee (1948) cut this to 16 years.
Wood's Despatch (1854) is the 'Magna Carta of English education in India'; Hunter Commission (1882) stressed primary education; Sadler Commission (1917–19) proposed 12 years of schooling.
Wardha Scheme of Basic Education (1937) was drafted by the Dr Zakir Husain Committee on Gandhi's Nai Talim idea.
National Education Day is 11 November (Maulana Abul Kalam Azad); Teachers' Day is 5 September (Dr S. Radhakrishnan); World Teachers' Day is 5 October.
Census 2011 literacy: 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%); Kerala highest (94.0%), Bihar lowest (61.8%); Delhi 86.2%.
SDGs were adopted in September 2015 (17 goals, 169 targets, horizon 2030); SDG 4 'Quality Education' has 10 targets.
RPwD Act 2016: 21 disabilities, benchmark disability 40%, 4% reservation in government posts, 5% seats in higher education, free education for children with benchmark disabilities aged 6–18.
Classical languages: 11 after Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali were added in October 2024; the Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages.
Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 States; IST is based on 82°30'E through Mirzapur (UP); India has 28 States and 8 UTs.
Demographic dividend: growth potential when the working-age (15–64) share of population exceeds the dependent share; needs investment in health, education and skills.
Vitamin deficiencies: A – night blindness; B1 – beri-beri; C – scurvy; D – rickets; iodine – goitre; iron – anaemia.
Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole on 23 Aug 2023; 23 August is National Space Day. Nobel Peace Prize 2025: María Corina Machado.

mcqs.q_en: Which Constitutional Amendment Act inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children of the age of six to fourteen years a Fundamental Right?
mcqs.q_hi: किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा अनुच्छेद 21A अंतःस्थापित किया गया, जिसने छह से चौदह वर्ष की आयु के बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा को मूल अधिकार बनाया?
mcqs.explain_en: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Art 21A (in force from 1 April 2010 with the RTE Act 2009), substituted Art 45 and added duty 51A(k). The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved education to the Concurrent List; the 93rd (2005) inserted Art 15(5) on reservation in private educational institutions.
mcqs.explain_hi: 86वें संशोधन अधिनियम, 2002 ने अनुच्छेद 21A जोड़ा (1 अप्रैल 2010 से शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम 2009 के साथ प्रवृत्त), अनुच्छेद 45 को प्रतिस्थापित किया और कर्तव्य 51A(k) जोड़ा। 42वें संशोधन (1976) ने शिक्षा को समवर्ती सूची में डाला; 93वें (2005) ने निजी शिक्षा संस्थानों में आरक्षण हेतु अनुच्छेद 15(5) जोड़ा।
mcqs.source: Constitution of India, Art 21A; Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 21A of the Constitution:
1. It provides for free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.
2. It came into force on 1 April 2010, the same day as the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009.
3. It is placed in Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21A के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. यह छह से चौदह वर्ष की आयु के सभी बच्चों को निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का प्रावधान करता है, ऐसी रीति से जैसी राज्य विधि द्वारा निर्धारित करे।
2. यह 1 अप्रैल 2010 को प्रवृत्त हुआ, उसी दिन जब निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 प्रवृत्त हुआ।
3. यह संविधान के भाग IV (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्त्व) में रखा गया है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: Statements 1 and 2 reproduce the text and commencement of Art 21A. Statement 3 is wrong: Art 21A is in Part III (Fundamental Rights); the related directive, Art 45, is in Part IV.
mcqs.explain_hi: कथन 1 और 2 अनुच्छेद 21A के पाठ और प्रवर्तन तिथि को सही बताते हैं। कथन 3 गलत है: अनुच्छेद 21A भाग III (मूल अधिकार) में है; संबंधित निदेशक तत्त्व अनुच्छेद 45 भाग IV में है।
mcqs.source: Constitution of India, Part III, Art 21A; MHRD notification bringing 86th Amendment into force w.e.f. 01.04.2010

mcqs.q_en: After the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, Article 45 directs the State to endeavour to provide:
mcqs.q_hi: संविधान (छियासीवाँ संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2002 के पश्चात् अनुच्छेद 45 राज्य को निम्नलिखित में से किसके लिए प्रयास करने का निदेश देता है?
options_en: free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of fourteen years
early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years
facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education
promotion of the educational interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
options_hi: चौदह वर्ष की आयु पूर्ण करने तक सभी बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा
छह वर्ष की आयु पूर्ण करने तक सभी बच्चों के लिए प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखरेख और शिक्षा
शिक्षा के प्राथमिक स्तर पर मातृभाषा में शिक्षा की सुविधाएँ
अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के शैक्षिक हितों की अभिवृद्धि
mcqs.explain_en: The substituted Art 45 covers early childhood care and education for children below six, since 6–14 moved to Art 21A. Option A is the original (pre-2002) Art 45; option C is Art 350A; option D is Art 46.
mcqs.explain_hi: प्रतिस्थापित अनुच्छेद 45 छह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों की प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखरेख और शिक्षा से संबंधित है, क्योंकि 6–14 आयु वर्ग अनुच्छेद 21A में चला गया। विकल्प A मूल (2002 से पूर्व) अनुच्छेद 45 है; विकल्प C अनुच्छेद 350A और विकल्प D अनुच्छेद 46 है।
mcqs.source: Constitution of India, Art 45 (as substituted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002)

mcqs.q_en:
Match List I (Article) with List II (Provision) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List I
A. Article 30
B. Article 46
C. Article 350A
D. Article 51A(k)
List II
1. Facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children of linguistic minority groups
2. Duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years
3. Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice
4. Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections
mcqs.q_hi:
सूची I (अनुच्छेद) को सूची II (प्रावधान) से सुमेलित कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए:
सूची I
A. अनुच्छेद 30
B. अनुच्छेद 46
C. अनुच्छेद 350A
D. अनुच्छेद 51A(k)
सूची II
1. भाषाई अल्पसंख्यक वर्गों के बालकों को प्राथमिक स्तर पर मातृभाषा में शिक्षा की सुविधाएँ
2. माता-पिता या संरक्षक का अपने छह से चौदह वर्ष की आयु के बालक या प्रतिपाल्य को शिक्षा के अवसर प्रदान करने का कर्तव्य
3. अल्पसंख्यकों का अपनी रुचि की शिक्षा संस्थाओं की स्थापना और प्रशासन का अधिकार
4. अनुसूचित जातियों, अनुसूचित जनजातियों और अन्य दुर्बल वर्गों के शिक्षा और अर्थ संबंधी हितों की अभिवृद्धि
mcqs.explain_en: Art 30 = minority educational institutions; Art 46 = SC/ST/weaker sections (a Directive Principle); Art 350A = mother-tongue instruction at primary stage; Art 51A(k) = parental duty. The distractors swap 350A with 46 or with 51A(k).
mcqs.explain_hi: अनुच्छेद 30 = अल्पसंख्यक शिक्षा संस्थाएँ; अनुच्छेद 46 = अनुसूचित जाति/जनजाति/दुर्बल वर्ग (नीति निदेशक तत्त्व); अनुच्छेद 350A = प्राथमिक स्तर पर मातृभाषा में शिक्षा; अनुच्छेद 51A(k) = माता-पिता का कर्तव्य। गलत विकल्पों में 350A को 46 या 51A(k) से बदल दिया गया है।
mcqs.source: Constitution of India, Arts 30, 46, 350A, 51A(k)

mcqs.q_en: 'Education' was transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List (Entry 25 of List III) of the Seventh Schedule by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
mcqs.q_hi: सातवीं अनुसूची में 'शिक्षा' को राज्य सूची से समवर्ती सूची (सूची III की प्रविष्टि 25) में किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा अंतरित किया गया?
mcqs.explain_en: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 shifted education (along with forests, weights and measures, administration of justice, and protection of wild animals and birds) to the Concurrent List. The 7th Amendment inserted Arts 350A/350B; the 86th inserted Art 21A.
mcqs.explain_hi: 42वें संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976 ने शिक्षा को (वन, माप-तौल, न्याय प्रशासन और वन्य जीव संरक्षण के साथ) समवर्ती सूची में अंतरित किया। 7वें संशोधन ने अनुच्छेद 350A/350B जोड़े; 86वें ने अनुच्छेद 21A जोड़ा।
mcqs.source: Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976; Seventh Schedule, List III, Entry 25

mcqs.q_en:
With reference to the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Entry 66 of the Union List deals with co-ordination and determination of standards in institutions for higher education or research and scientific and technical institutions.
2. Entry 25 of the Concurrent List covers education, including technical education, medical education and universities, subject to Entries 63 to 66 of the Union List.
3. 'Vocational and technical training of labour' is also included in Entry 25 of the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
संविधान की सातवीं अनुसूची के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. संघ सूची की प्रविष्टि 66 उच्चतर शिक्षा या अनुसंधान संस्थाओं तथा वैज्ञानिक और तकनीकी संस्थाओं में मानकों के समन्वय और अवधारण से संबंधित है।
2. समवर्ती सूची की प्रविष्टि 25 में शिक्षा, जिसमें तकनीकी शिक्षा, आयुर्विज्ञान शिक्षा और विश्वविद्यालय सम्मिलित हैं, संघ सूची की प्रविष्टियों 63 से 66 के अधीन रहते हुए आती है।
3. 'श्रमिकों का व्यावसायिक और तकनीकी प्रशिक्षण' भी समवर्ती सूची की प्रविष्टि 25 में सम्मिलित है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: Entry 25, List III reads: 'Education, including technical education, medical education and universities, subject to the provisions of entries 63, 64, 65 and 66 of List I; vocational and technical training of labour.' Entry 66, List I is the standards-coordination entry under which UGC and similar bodies legislate. All three statements are correct.
mcqs.explain_hi: सूची III की प्रविष्टि 25 है: 'शिक्षा, जिसमें तकनीकी शिक्षा, आयुर्विज्ञान शिक्षा और विश्वविद्यालय सम्मिलित हैं, सूची I की प्रविष्टियों 63, 64, 65 और 66 के उपबंधों के अधीन रहते हुए; श्रमिकों का व्यावसायिक और तकनीकी प्रशिक्षण।' सूची I की प्रविष्टि 66 मानकों के समन्वय की प्रविष्टि है जिसके अधीन UGC जैसे निकाय बनाए गए हैं। तीनों कथन सही हैं।
mcqs.source: Constitution of India, Seventh Schedule, List I Entry 66; List III Entry 25

mcqs.q_en: Under Article 51A(k) of the Constitution, the duty to provide opportunities for education to a child between the age of six and fourteen years is cast upon:
mcqs.q_hi: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 51A(k) के अंतर्गत छह से चौदह वर्ष की आयु के बालक को शिक्षा के अवसर प्रदान करने का कर्तव्य किस पर अधिरोपित है?
mcqs.explain_en: Art 51A(k), added by the 86th Amendment, makes it a Fundamental Duty of the parent or guardian. The State's corresponding obligation is in Art 21A; duties of local authorities and SMCs flow from the RTE Act 2009, not from Art 51A.
mcqs.explain_hi: 86वें संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया अनुच्छेद 51A(k) इसे माता-पिता या संरक्षक का मूल कर्तव्य बनाता है। राज्य का तत्संबंधी दायित्व अनुच्छेद 21A में है; स्थानीय प्राधिकारी और विद्यालय प्रबंधन समिति के कर्तव्य शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम 2009 से आते हैं, अनुच्छेद 51A से नहीं।
mcqs.source: Constitution of India, Art 51A(k)

mcqs.q_en:
Assertion (A): The Fundamental Duties under Article 51A are not directly enforceable by courts.
Reason (R): The Fundamental Duties were added by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mcqs.q_hi:
अभिकथन (A): अनुच्छेद 51A के अंतर्गत मूल कर्तव्य न्यायालयों द्वारा प्रत्यक्षतः प्रवर्तनीय नहीं हैं।
कारण (R): मूल कर्तव्यों को स्वर्ण सिंह समिति की संस्तुति पर संविधान (बयालीसवाँ संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1976 द्वारा जोड़ा गया था।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए:
options_en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
options_hi: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है
A और R दोनों सही हैं परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
A सही है परंतु R गलत है
A गलत है परंतु R सही है
mcqs.explain_en: Both statements are factually true: duties are non-justiciable, and they were inserted in 1976 on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice. But their non-enforceability stems from the absence of any legal sanction in Part IVA, not from the manner or year of their insertion, so R does not explain A.
mcqs.explain_hi: दोनों कथन तथ्यात्मक रूप से सही हैं: कर्तव्य न्यायालय द्वारा प्रवर्तनीय नहीं हैं और वे स्वर्ण सिंह समिति की सलाह पर 1976 में जोड़े गए। परंतु उनकी अप्रवर्तनीयता भाग IVA में किसी विधिक दंड के न होने से है, न कि उन्हें जोड़ने की रीति या वर्ष से; अतः R, A की व्याख्या नहीं करता।
mcqs.source: Constitution of India, Part IVA, Art 51A; 42nd Amendment Act, 1976

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the National Capital Territory of Delhi:
1. Article 239AA was inserted by the Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991.
2. The Legislative Assembly of the NCT of Delhi has 70 members.
3. The Legislative Assembly of Delhi is competent to make laws on 'Police' (Entry 2 of the State List).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. अनुच्छेद 239AA संविधान (उनहत्तरवाँ संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1991 द्वारा अंतःस्थापित किया गया।
2. राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली की विधान सभा में 70 सदस्य हैं।
3. दिल्ली विधान सभा 'पुलिस' (राज्य सूची की प्रविष्टि 2) पर विधि बनाने के लिए सक्षम है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: The 69th Amendment (1991) inserted Arts 239AA and 239AB and the Assembly has 70 seats. Under Art 239AA(3)(a) the Assembly cannot legislate on Entries 1 (public order), 2 (police) and 18 (land) of the State List, so statement 3 is wrong.
mcqs.explain_hi: 69वें संशोधन (1991) ने अनुच्छेद 239AA और 239AB जोड़े और विधान सभा में 70 सीटें हैं। अनुच्छेद 239AA(3)(a) के अनुसार विधान सभा राज्य सूची की प्रविष्टि 1 (लोक व्यवस्था), 2 (पुलिस) और 18 (भूमि) पर विधि नहीं बना सकती, अतः कथन 3 गलत है।
mcqs.source: Constitution of India, Art 239AA; Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991; GNCTD Act, 1991

mcqs.q_en: The elected members of the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi were included in the electoral college for the election of the President of India by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
mcqs.q_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति के निर्वाचन हेतु निर्वाचक मंडल में राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली की विधान सभा के निर्वाचित सदस्यों को किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा सम्मिलित किया गया?
mcqs.explain_en: The 70th Amendment Act, 1992 amended Art 54 so that 'State' includes the NCT of Delhi and Puducherry for the Presidential electoral college. The 69th created Delhi's Assembly; the 73rd and 74th deal with Panchayats and Municipalities.
mcqs.explain_hi: 70वें संशोधन अधिनियम, 1992 ने अनुच्छेद 54 में संशोधन कर राष्ट्रपति के निर्वाचक मंडल के प्रयोजन से 'राज्य' में दिल्ली और पुडुचेरी को सम्मिलित किया। 69वें ने दिल्ली की विधान सभा बनाई; 73वाँ और 74वाँ पंचायतों और नगरपालिकाओं से संबंधित हैं।
mcqs.source: Constitution (Seventieth Amendment) Act, 1992; Art 54 Explanation

mcqs.q_en: The observation "the destiny of India is now being shaped in her classrooms" is associated with which Commission?
mcqs.q_hi: "भारत की नियति अब उसकी कक्षाओं में गढ़ी जा रही है" — यह कथन किस आयोग से संबद्ध है?
mcqs.explain_en: The sentence opens the report of the Education Commission 1964–66 (Kothari Commission), 'Education and National Development'. The 1948–49 body is the Radhakrishnan Commission, 1952–53 the Mudaliar Commission and 1882 the Hunter Commission.
mcqs.explain_hi: यह वाक्य शिक्षा आयोग 1964–66 (कोठारी आयोग) की रिपोर्ट 'शिक्षा और राष्ट्रीय विकास' का प्रारंभिक वाक्य है। 1948–49 का आयोग राधाकृष्णन आयोग, 1952–53 का मुदालियर आयोग और 1882 का हंटर आयोग है।
mcqs.source: Report of the Education Commission 1964–66 (Kothari Commission), Chapter 1

mcqs.q_en:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):
1. Hunter Commission
2. Sargent Report
3. Wood's Despatch
4. Sadler Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mcqs.q_hi:
निम्नलिखित को कालानुक्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए (सबसे पहले वाला प्रथम):
1. हंटर आयोग
2. सार्जेंट रिपोर्ट
3. वुड का घोषणा-पत्र (वुड्स डिस्पैच)
4. सैडलर आयोग
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए:
mcqs.explain_en: Wood's Despatch 1854, Hunter Commission 1882, Sadler (Calcutta University) Commission 1917–19, Sargent Report 1944. The Hartog Committee (1929) and Wardha Scheme (1937) fall between Sadler and Sargent.
mcqs.explain_hi: वुड्स डिस्पैच 1854, हंटर आयोग 1882, सैडलर (कलकत्ता विश्वविद्यालय) आयोग 1917–19, सार्जेंट रिपोर्ट 1944। हार्टोग समिति (1929) और वर्धा योजना (1937) सैडलर और सार्जेंट के बीच आती हैं।
mcqs.source: Standard history of education in India (NCERT / J.C. Aggarwal)

mcqs.q_en:
Match List I (Commission/Committee) with List II (Main concern) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List I
A. Radhakrishnan Commission
B. Mudaliar Commission
C. Acharya Ramamurti Committee
D. Yashpal Committee (1993)
List II
1. Secondary education
2. 'Learning without Burden'
3. University education
4. Review of the National Policy on Education, 1986
mcqs.q_hi:
सूची I (आयोग/समिति) को सूची II (मुख्य विषय) से सुमेलित कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए:
सूची I
A. राधाकृष्णन आयोग
B. मुदालियर आयोग
C. आचार्य राममूर्ति समिति
D. यशपाल समिति (1993)
सूची II
1. माध्यमिक शिक्षा
2. 'बोझ के बिना शिक्षा' (लर्निंग विदाउट बर्डन)
3. विश्वविद्यालय शिक्षा
4. राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति, 1986 की समीक्षा
mcqs.explain_en: Radhakrishnan Commission 1948–49 = University Education Commission; Mudaliar Commission 1952–53 = Secondary Education Commission; Acharya Ramamurti Committee 1990 reviewed NPE 1986 ('Towards an Enlightened and Humane Society'); Yashpal Committee 1993 produced 'Learning without Burden'.
mcqs.explain_hi: राधाकृष्णन आयोग 1948–49 = विश्वविद्यालय शिक्षा आयोग; मुदालियर आयोग 1952–53 = माध्यमिक शिक्षा आयोग; आचार्य राममूर्ति समिति 1990 ने NPE 1986 की समीक्षा की ('प्रबुद्ध और मानवीय समाज की ओर'); यशपाल समिति 1993 ने 'लर्निंग विदाउट बर्डन' रिपोर्ट दी।
mcqs.source: Standard history of Indian education policy; MHRD/NCERT records

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the National Policy on Education (NPE), 1986:
1. It was adopted in 1986 and revised in 1992 on the basis of a Programme of Action.
2. Operation Blackboard and Navodaya Vidyalayas were initiatives flowing from it.
3. It proposed the 10+2+3 pattern of education for the first time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति (NPE), 1986 के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. इसे 1986 में अपनाया गया और 1992 में कार्य योजना (प्रोग्राम ऑफ एक्शन) के आधार पर संशोधित किया गया।
2. ऑपरेशन ब्लैकबोर्ड और नवोदय विद्यालय इसी से निकली पहलें थीं।
3. इसने पहली बार 10+2+3 शिक्षा संरचना का प्रस्ताव किया।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: NPE 1986 (Rajiv Gandhi government) was modified in 1992 after the Ramamurti review and the Janardhana Reddy CABE committee, and launched Operation Blackboard and Navodaya Vidyalayas. The 10+2+3 structure was recommended by the Kothari Commission and adopted in NPE 1968, so statement 3 is wrong.
mcqs.explain_hi: NPE 1986 (राजीव गांधी सरकार) को राममूर्ति समीक्षा और जनार्दन रेड्डी CABE समिति के बाद 1992 में संशोधित किया गया; इसने ऑपरेशन ब्लैकबोर्ड और नवोदय विद्यालय आरंभ किए। 10+2+3 संरचना कोठारी आयोग ने सुझाई और NPE 1968 में अपनाई गई, अतः कथन 3 गलत है।
mcqs.source: National Policy on Education 1986 (as modified in 1992); Programme of Action 1992

mcqs.q_en: The Sargent Report (1944) on 'Post-War Educational Development in India' envisaged universal, compulsory and free education for children aged 6–14 years to be achieved within a period of:
mcqs.q_hi: 'भारत में युद्धोत्तर शैक्षिक विकास' पर सार्जेंट रिपोर्ट (1944) ने 6–14 वर्ष के बच्चों के लिए सार्वभौमिक, अनिवार्य और निःशुल्क शिक्षा को कितनी अवधि में प्राप्त करने की परिकल्पना की थी?
mcqs.explain_en: The CABE scheme prepared under John Sargent set a 40-year horizon (to about 1984). The Kher Committee (1948) considered this too long and proposed 16 years, which is the trap option.
mcqs.explain_hi: जॉन सार्जेंट के अधीन तैयार CABE योजना ने 40 वर्ष (लगभग 1984 तक) की अवधि रखी। खेर समिति (1948) ने इसे अधिक मानते हुए 16 वर्ष सुझाए, जो यहाँ भ्रमित करने वाला विकल्प है।
mcqs.source: CABE Report 'Post-War Educational Development in India' (Sargent Report), 1944; Kher Committee 1948

mcqs.q_en: The Wardha Scheme of Basic Education (Nai Talim), 1937, was formulated by a committee headed by:
mcqs.q_hi: बुनियादी शिक्षा की वर्धा योजना (नई तालीम), 1937 को जिस समिति ने तैयार किया, उसके अध्यक्ष कौन थे?
mcqs.explain_en: After the Wardha conference of October 1937, Gandhi's proposals were worked into a scheme by the Dr Zakir Husain Committee (craft-centred, self-supporting education for ages 7–14). B.G. Kher chaired the later 1948 committee on the Sargent timeline.
mcqs.explain_hi: अक्टूबर 1937 के वर्धा सम्मेलन के बाद गांधीजी के प्रस्तावों को डॉ. ज़ाकिर हुसैन समिति ने योजना का रूप दिया (7–14 आयु के लिए शिल्प-केंद्रित, स्वावलंबी शिक्षा)। बी.जी. खेर ने बाद में 1948 की समिति की अध्यक्षता की।
mcqs.source: Zakir Husain Committee Report on Basic National Education, 1938

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about education under British rule:
1. The Charter Act of 1813 set apart a sum of not less than one lakh rupees a year for education in India.
2. Macaulay's Minute of 1835 favoured the promotion of oriental learning through Sanskrit and Arabic.
3. Wood's Despatch of 1854 recommended the establishment of universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
ब्रिटिश शासन में शिक्षा के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. 1813 के चार्टर अधिनियम ने भारत में शिक्षा के लिए प्रतिवर्ष कम से कम एक लाख रुपये की राशि निर्धारित की।
2. मैकाले के 1835 के विवरण-पत्र (मिनट) ने संस्कृत और अरबी के माध्यम से प्राच्य विद्या के संवर्धन का समर्थन किया।
3. 1854 के वुड्स डिस्पैच ने कलकत्ता, बंबई और मद्रास में विश्वविद्यालयों की स्थापना की संस्तुति की।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: The 1813 Charter Act's one-lakh clause was the first State commitment to education, and Wood's Despatch led to the three universities of 1857. Macaulay's Minute argued the opposite of statement 2: it backed English and Western learning over oriental studies.
mcqs.explain_hi: 1813 के चार्टर अधिनियम का एक लाख रुपये का उपबंध शिक्षा के प्रति पहली राजकीय प्रतिबद्धता था, और वुड्स डिस्पैच से 1857 के तीन विश्वविद्यालय बने। मैकाले के मिनट ने कथन 2 के विपरीत प्राच्य विद्या के बजाय अंग्रेज़ी और पाश्चात्य ज्ञान का समर्थन किया।
mcqs.source: Charter Act 1813; Macaulay's Minute 1835; Wood's Despatch 1854 (standard modern Indian history)

mcqs.q_en: As of 2026, how many languages have been accorded the status of 'Classical Language' by the Government of India?
mcqs.q_hi: 2026 की स्थिति में भारत सरकार द्वारा कितनी भाषाओं को 'शास्त्रीय भाषा' का दर्जा दिया गया है?
mcqs.explain_en: Six languages held the status till 2024: Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014). The Union Cabinet added Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali on 3 October 2024, taking the total to 11. '6' is the pre-2024 figure.
mcqs.explain_hi: 2024 तक छह भाषाओं को यह दर्जा था: तमिल (2004), संस्कृत (2005), तेलुगु और कन्नड़ (2008), मलयालम (2013), ओड़िया (2014)। केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल ने 3 अक्टूबर 2024 को मराठी, पालि, प्राकृत, असमिया और बांग्ला को जोड़ा, जिससे कुल संख्या 11 हो गई। '6' 2024 से पूर्व की संख्या है।
mcqs.source: Union Cabinet decision, 3 Oct 2024 (PIB); Ministry of Culture

mcqs.q_en: Which of the following monuments in Delhi is NOT inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
mcqs.q_hi: दिल्ली के निम्नलिखित स्मारकों में से कौन-सा यूनेस्को विश्व विरासत सूची में सम्मिलित नहीं है?
mcqs.explain_en: Delhi has three World Heritage Sites: Qutb Minar and its Monuments (1993), Humayun's Tomb (1993) and the Red Fort Complex (2007). The Jantar Mantar that is inscribed (2010) is the one at Jaipur, not Delhi.
mcqs.explain_hi: दिल्ली में तीन विश्व विरासत स्थल हैं: कुतुब मीनार और उसके स्मारक (1993), हुमायूँ का मकबरा (1993) और लाल किला परिसर (2007)। सूची में सम्मिलित जंतर मंतर (2010) जयपुर का है, दिल्ली का नहीं।
mcqs.source: UNESCO World Heritage List (whc.unesco.org), India entries

mcqs.q_en: National Education Day (11 November) is observed to commemorate the birth anniversary of:
mcqs.q_hi: राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा दिवस (11 नवंबर) किसकी जयंती के उपलक्ष्य में मनाया जाता है?
mcqs.explain_en: Maulana Azad, independent India's first Education Minister (1947–58), was born on 11 November 1888; the day has been observed as National Education Day since 2008. Radhakrishnan's birthday (5 September) is Teachers' Day.
mcqs.explain_hi: स्वतंत्र भारत के प्रथम शिक्षा मंत्री (1947–58) मौलाना आज़ाद का जन्म 11 नवंबर 1888 को हुआ; 2008 से यह दिन राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा दिवस के रूप में मनाया जाता है। राधाकृष्णन की जयंती (5 सितंबर) शिक्षक दिवस है।
mcqs.source: MHRD decision, 2008 (National Education Day)

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements about Delhi:
1. The decision to shift the capital of British India from Calcutta to Delhi was announced at the Delhi Durbar of 1911.
2. The Delhi High Court was established in 1966.
3. Delhi is represented by 7 members in the Lok Sabha and 5 members in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
दिल्ली के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. ब्रिटिश भारत की राजधानी कलकत्ता से दिल्ली स्थानांतरित करने की घोषणा 1911 के दिल्ली दरबार में की गई।
2. दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय की स्थापना 1966 में हुई।
3. दिल्ली का प्रतिनिधित्व लोक सभा में 7 और राज्य सभा में 5 सदस्य करते हैं।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: George V announced the transfer at the Delhi Durbar on 12 December 1911 (New Delhi was inaugurated in 1931), and the Delhi High Court began on 31 October 1966 under the Delhi High Court Act, 1966. Delhi has 7 Lok Sabha seats but only 3 Rajya Sabha seats, so statement 3 is wrong.
mcqs.explain_hi: जॉर्ज पंचम ने 12 दिसंबर 1911 के दिल्ली दरबार में स्थानांतरण की घोषणा की (नई दिल्ली का उद्घाटन 1931 में हुआ), और दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय अधिनियम, 1966 के अधीन 31 अक्टूबर 1966 से दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय आरंभ हुआ। दिल्ली की लोक सभा में 7 सीटें हैं परंतु राज्य सभा में केवल 3, अतः कथन 3 गलत है।
mcqs.source: Delhi High Court Act, 1966; Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Schedules); standard Delhi history

mcqs.q_en:
Match List I (Historic city of Delhi) with List II (Founder) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List I
A. Siri
B. Tughlaqabad
C. Dinpanah
D. Shahjahanabad
List II
1. Humayun
2. Alauddin Khalji
3. Shah Jahan
4. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq
mcqs.q_hi:
सूची I (दिल्ली का ऐतिहासिक नगर) को सूची II (संस्थापक) से सुमेलित कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए:
सूची I
A. सीरी
B. तुगलकाबाद
C. दीनपनाह
D. शाहजहाँनाबाद
सूची II
1. हुमायूँ
2. अलाउद्दीन खिलजी
3. शाहजहाँ
4. गयासुद्दीन तुगलक
mcqs.explain_en: Siri was built by Alauddin Khalji (c. 1303), Tughlaqabad by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (1321), Dinpanah (Purana Qila) by Humayun (1533) and Shahjahanabad by Shah Jahan (1639). Jahanpanah (Muhammad bin Tughlaq) and Firozabad (Firoz Shah Tughlaq) are the other Sultanate cities.
mcqs.explain_hi: सीरी अलाउद्दीन खिलजी (लगभग 1303), तुगलकाबाद गयासुद्दीन तुगलक (1321), दीनपनाह (पुराना किला) हुमायूँ (1533) और शाहजहाँनाबाद शाहजहाँ (1639) ने बनवाया। जहाँपनाह (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक) और फिरोजाबाद (फिरोज शाह तुगलक) सल्तनत काल के अन्य नगर हैं।
mcqs.source: Standard medieval Indian history (NCERT); ASI Delhi Circle

mcqs.q_en: The principal statute regulating recognised schools in Delhi, under which the Delhi School Education Rules were framed, is the Delhi School Education Act, ______.
mcqs.q_hi: दिल्ली में मान्यता प्राप्त विद्यालयों को विनियमित करने वाला प्रमुख अधिनियम, जिसके अधीन दिल्ली विद्यालय शिक्षा नियम बनाए गए, दिल्ली विद्यालय शिक्षा अधिनियम, ______ है।
mcqs.explain_en: The Delhi School Education Act, 1973 (Act 18 of 1973) and the Delhi School Education Rules, 1973 govern recognition, management, service conditions of employees, admissions and fees in Delhi schools. 1966 is the year of the Delhi High Court Act; 1986 is the NPE year.
mcqs.explain_hi: दिल्ली विद्यालय शिक्षा अधिनियम, 1973 (1973 का अधिनियम 18) और दिल्ली विद्यालय शिक्षा नियम, 1973 दिल्ली के विद्यालयों की मान्यता, प्रबंधन, कर्मचारियों की सेवा शर्तें, प्रवेश और फीस को नियंत्रित करते हैं। 1966 दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय अधिनियम का वर्ष है; 1986 NPE का वर्ष है।
mcqs.source: Delhi School Education Act, 1973 (Act 18 of 1973); edudel.nic.in

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Capital Territory of Delhi shares its boundary only with the States of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.
2. The Delhi Ridge is a northern extension of the Aravalli Range.
3. The Tropic of Cancer passes through Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली की सीमा केवल हरियाणा और उत्तर प्रदेश राज्यों से लगती है।
2. दिल्ली रिज अरावली पर्वतमाला का उत्तरी विस्तार है।
3. कर्क रेखा दिल्ली से होकर गुजरती है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: Delhi is bounded by Haryana on the north, west and south and by Uttar Pradesh on the east, and the Ridge is the tail of the Aravallis. The Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) passes through eight States (Gujarat to Mizoram); Delhi lies at about 28.6°N.
mcqs.explain_hi: दिल्ली के उत्तर, पश्चिम और दक्षिण में हरियाणा तथा पूर्व में उत्तर प्रदेश है, और रिज अरावली का अंतिम भाग है। कर्क रेखा (23°30' उत्तर) आठ राज्यों (गुजरात से मिज़ोरम) से गुजरती है; दिल्ली लगभग 28.6° उत्तर पर स्थित है।
mcqs.source: NCERT Class 9 'Contemporary India I', Ch 1; Survey of India

mcqs.q_en: The recommendation that public expenditure on education be raised to 6 per cent of the national income/GDP was first made by:
mcqs.q_hi: शिक्षा पर सार्वजनिक व्यय को राष्ट्रीय आय/सकल घरेलू उत्पाद के 6 प्रतिशत तक बढ़ाने की संस्तुति सबसे पहले किसने की?
mcqs.explain_en: The Kothari Commission recommended raising education spending to 6 per cent of national income by 1985–86. NPE 1968 adopted the target, NPE 1986/1992 repeated it and NEP 2020 (para 26) reaffirms it, so the policies are later echoes, not the origin.
mcqs.explain_hi: कोठारी आयोग ने 1985–86 तक शिक्षा व्यय को राष्ट्रीय आय के 6 प्रतिशत तक बढ़ाने की संस्तुति की। NPE 1968 ने इसे अपनाया, NPE 1986/1992 ने दोहराया और NEP 2020 (पैरा 26) इसकी पुनः पुष्टि करती है; अतः नीतियाँ बाद की पुनरावृत्ति हैं, मूल स्रोत नहीं।
mcqs.source: Report of the Education Commission 1964–66; NPE 1968; NEP 2020 para 26

mcqs.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):
1. SDG 4 is 'Quality Education', with 2030 as the target year.
2. SDG 4 has 10 targets (4.1 to 4.7 and 4.a to 4.c).
3. The SDGs were adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in September 2000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
सतत विकास लक्ष्यों (SDGs) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. SDG 4 'गुणवत्तापूर्ण शिक्षा' है, जिसका लक्ष्य वर्ष 2030 है।
2. SDG 4 के 10 लक्ष्य हैं (4.1 से 4.7 और 4.a से 4.c)।
3. SDGs को संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा ने सितंबर 2000 में अपनाया था।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: SDG 4 ('Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all') has seven outcome targets and three means-of-implementation targets. The 17 SDGs were adopted in September 2015 as the 2030 Agenda; September 2000 was the Millennium Declaration that produced the MDGs.
mcqs.explain_hi: SDG 4 ('समावेशी और समतामूलक गुणवत्तापूर्ण शिक्षा सुनिश्चित करना और सभी के लिए जीवनपर्यंत सीखने के अवसरों को बढ़ावा देना') के सात परिणाम लक्ष्य और तीन कार्यान्वयन-साधन लक्ष्य हैं। 17 SDGs सितंबर 2015 में 2030 एजेंडा के रूप में अपनाए गए; सितंबर 2000 में सहस्राब्दि घोषणा हुई थी जिससे MDGs बने।
mcqs.source: UN General Assembly Resolution 70/1 (25 Sept 2015), 'Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda'

mcqs.q_en: According to Census 2011, the literacy rate of India (population aged 7 years and above) was:
mcqs.q_hi: जनगणना 2011 के अनुसार भारत की साक्षरता दर (7 वर्ष और उससे अधिक आयु की जनसंख्या) कितनी थी?
mcqs.explain_en: Census 2011 recorded 74.04% literacy (male 82.14%, female 65.46%), up from 64.8% in Census 2001. Kerala was highest (94.0%) and Bihar lowest (61.8%); Delhi stood at 86.2%.
mcqs.source: Census of India 2011, Provisional/Final Population Totals (ORGI)

mcqs.q_en:
Assertion (A): India is said to be passing through a phase of 'demographic dividend'.
Reason (R): The share of the working-age population (15–64 years) in India's total population is larger than the share of the dependent population (children and the elderly).
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mcqs.q_hi:
अभिकथन (A): कहा जाता है कि भारत 'जनसांख्यिकीय लाभांश' के चरण से गुजर रहा है।
कारण (R): भारत की कुल जनसंख्या में कार्यशील आयु (15–64 वर्ष) की जनसंख्या का अनुपात आश्रित जनसंख्या (बच्चे और वृद्ध) के अनुपात से अधिक है।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए:
options_en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
options_hi: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है
A और R दोनों सही हैं परंतु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
A सही है परंतु R गलत है
A गलत है परंतु R सही है
mcqs.explain_en: A demographic dividend is precisely the growth potential created when the working-age share rises relative to dependents (a falling dependency ratio); India's median age is about 28 and this window is expected to last to the mid-2050s. R states the defining condition, so it explains A.
mcqs.explain_hi: जनसांख्यिकीय लाभांश वही वृद्धि-संभावना है जो कार्यशील आयु वर्ग का अनुपात आश्रितों की तुलना में बढ़ने (घटते आश्रितता अनुपात) से बनती है; भारत की माध्यिका आयु लगभग 28 है और यह अवसर 2050 के दशक के मध्य तक रहने की संभावना है। R परिभाषित करने वाली शर्त बताता है, अतः वह A की व्याख्या है।
mcqs.source: Standard concept (UNFPA; Economic Survey chapters on demography)

mcqs.q_en:
With reference to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. The Act recognises 21 specified disabilities.
2. It provides for 3 per cent reservation in vacancies in government establishments for persons with benchmark disabilities.
3. Every child with benchmark disability between the age of 6 and 18 years has the right to free education in a neighbourhood school or a special school.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.q_hi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. अधिनियम 21 विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं को मान्यता देता है।
2. यह बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले व्यक्तियों के लिए सरकारी स्थापनों की रिक्तियों में 3 प्रतिशत आरक्षण का प्रावधान करता है।
3. 6 से 18 वर्ष की आयु के बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले प्रत्येक बालक को पड़ोस के विद्यालय या विशेष विद्यालय में निःशुल्क शिक्षा का अधिकार है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
mcqs.explain_en: The Schedule lists 21 disabilities and Sec 31 gives children with benchmark disabilities (6–18) free education. Sec 34 fixes reservation in government posts at 4 per cent (3 per cent was the PwD Act 1995 figure), and Sec 32 reserves 5 per cent of seats in government and aided higher education institutions.
mcqs.explain_hi: अनुसूची में 21 दिव्यांगताएँ हैं और धारा 31 बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले बालकों (6–18) को निःशुल्क शिक्षा देती है। धारा 34 सरकारी पदों में आरक्षण 4 प्रतिशत निर्धारित करती है (3 प्रतिशत 1995 के अधिनियम का आँकड़ा था), और धारा 32 सरकारी एवं सहायता प्राप्त उच्च शिक्षा संस्थानों में 5 प्रतिशत सीटें आरक्षित करती है।
mcqs.source: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, Secs 31, 32, 34 and the Schedule

mcqs.q_en:
Match List I (Vitamin) with List II (Deficiency disease) and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List I
A. Vitamin A
B. Vitamin C
C. Vitamin D
D. Vitamin B1
List II
1. Scurvy
2. Rickets
3. Beri-beri
4. Night blindness
mcqs.q_hi:
सूची I (विटामिन) को सूची II (हीनता रोग) से सुमेलित कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए:
सूची I
A. विटामिन A
B. विटामिन C
C. विटामिन D
D. विटामिन B1
सूची II
1. स्कर्वी
2. रिकेट्स (सूखा रोग)
3. बेरी-बेरी
4. रतौंधी
mcqs.explain_en: Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency causes night blindness; vitamin C (ascorbic acid) scurvy; vitamin D rickets in children (osteomalacia in adults); vitamin B1 (thiamine) beri-beri. Mid-day meal and school health programmes target exactly these deficiencies.
mcqs.explain_hi: विटामिन A (रेटिनॉल) की कमी से रतौंधी; विटामिन C (एस्कॉर्बिक अम्ल) से स्कर्वी; विटामिन D से बच्चों में रिकेट्स (वयस्कों में ऑस्टियोमलेशिया); विटामिन B1 (थायमिन) से बेरी-बेरी होता है। मध्याह्न भोजन और विद्यालय स्वास्थ्य कार्यक्रम इन्हीं कमियों को लक्षित करते हैं।
mcqs.source: NCERT Science Class 6 'Components of Food'; standard nutrition facts
